description: >-
  Use in your first conversation with a new owner, or whenever they ask to set
  up (or redo the setup of) a photo-mosaic gallery website and no gallery is

  followed by build, preview, deploy and an optional daily auto-update routine.
---
# Getting started: set up the owner's mosaic gallery

You are about to build the owner a website where their photos form a shape (a heart, a state outline, their initials...). Greet them in one or two friendly sentences, say it takes about eight quick questions, then **ask exactly ONE question per message** and wait for the answer. Offer concrete options and a sensible default so they can answer in a few words ("any is fine" -> use the default). Skip a question the owner already answered. Keep every message short; no jargon.

## The questions (in this order)
1. **Photo source.** "Where should the photos come from? (a) an X/Twitter account's own posts (I read public posts - what's the @handle?), (b) photos you send me here in chat, or (c) a folder / Google Drive / Photos link (send the link or path)." Note the handle or folder. Only the owner's own account/photos. Tell them the finished gallery is public.
2. **Theme.** "What should count? e.g. nature, pets, travel, family, food, or anything - and is there anything I should leave out (screenshots, people, memes...)?" Default: everything except screenshots/memes/documents.
3. **Time range.** "Which time range? e.g. this year, last 12 months, or everything." Convert to `since`/`until` dates (default: from Jan 1 of the current year).
4. **Title + caption.** "What should the gallery be called, and what short caption goes under it?" Offer to suggest 2-3 titles from their theme; one-liner caption.
5. **Accent colour.** "What accent colour (a colour name or hex)?" Default a blue `#2f7bd9`. Convert names to hex; must be readable on near-black.
6. **Shape.** "What shape should the mosaic form? heart, circle, star, a bird, an outline of a US state or any country, their initials or a word, or a silhouette of something (describe it or send an image)." For a state/country: which one. For letters: which text (short is best, 1-4 letters, `/` for a second line). For a described silhouette: find or ask for a clean image and use `image:` (see `build-mosaic-gallery`). Mention that sparse galleries show a few repeated photos that get replaced as new ones arrive.
7. **Hosting.** "I'll publish it on Vercel (free). You'll need to sign in once: I'll send you a link and a code to approve - takes 30 seconds. Do you have a Vercel account (a free one can be created at vercel.com with email/GitHub/Google), or would you prefer another host?" Ask the name they'd like in the address (e.g. `summer-memories` -> summer-memories.vercel.app).
8. **Daily update.** "Want me to check every evening for new photos and add them automatically? I'll only message you when something was added. What time (and your time zone)? Default 8:00 PM." 

## After the last answer
1. **Save to memory** (your memory tool) - key facts only: gallery dir `~/gallery`; source type + handle/folder; theme + exclusions; date range; title; caption; accent; shape; hosting (host, project name, public URL once known); routine time/zone/id; "gallery skills: build-mosaic-gallery, daily-gallery-update"; owner's preferences about photos (what they liked/rejected).
2. Tell them you're starting ("Give me a few minutes to collect and look at your photos").
3. **Build** with the `build-mosaic-gallery` skill (sections 0-4): write the code, `config` from the answers, fetch, de-duplicate, look at every contact sheet and decide by theme, apply. If fewer than ~12 photos match, say so and widen with the owner (time range/theme) or wait for more.
4. **Preview**: serve locally, take desktop + phone screenshots and the `card.png` share image (section 5), look at them yourself first, fix problems, then send them to the owner with the count. Ask: "Happy with this, or change the title, colour or shape?" Apply changes via `config` + `build` (`--regrid` for a new shape) and re-preview. Iterate until they approve.
5. **Deploy** (section 6): login handoff (send the sign-in link, wait for approval), `deploy`, `live-check`, view the live screenshot, send the owner the live link plus a tip to paste it in a post/message to see the share card.
6. **Routine**: if they said yes in question 8, create it exactly as described in `daily-gallery-update` ("Creating the routine"), run it once to test, save its id in memory.
7. **Recap** in 4-5 lines: link, how many photos, what the shape/theme is, when the daily update runs (or that it's off), and how to ask for changes ("just tell me: new shape, new title, add this photo, pause updates").

## Later requests
Change title/caption/colour: `config` + `build` + deploy. New shape: `config shape=...`, `build --regrid`, preview, deploy. Add specific photos they send: save into `~/gallery/inbox`, run the normal fetch/apply flow. Remove photos: ask first (tiles reshuffle), then `python3 gallery.py remove <idx|file-part|post-id>` and deploy. Pause/stop updates: delete the routine.

skills.name: daily-gallery-update
skills.description: Use for the recurring evening routine that keeps a photo-mosaic gallery up to date (find the owner's new photos, strictly de-duplicate, keep only those matching their theme, add them without moving existing tiles, redeploy, verify live) and when creating, editing or debugging that routine. Requires the gallery to be already built (see build-mosaic-gallery).

# Daily gallery update

Work in `~/gallery` (code from `build-mosaic-gallery`, `config.json` holds title/theme/handle/url). Mechanical work is done by `gallery.py`; you only look at pictures and decide. Be quiet: message the owner **only when photos were added** (or when something is broken and you could not fix it). Never ask questions in an unattended run - when unsure about a photo, skip it.

## Procedure
1. **Fetch new photos** since the last run:
   - X source: `python3 gallery.py fetch` (handle from config; scans back 3 days from the newest known photo; media already in the manifest is ignored). Exit code 2 = fxtwitter blocked -> use the X read tool fallback described in `build-mosaic-gallery` section 2 (`--x-json`).
   - Folder/chat-upload source: photos the owner sent since the last run are in `~/gallery/inbox` (save any chat photos there when they arrive); `python3 gallery.py fetch --folder ~/gallery/inbox`.
   If it prints `pending: 0` -> **stop silently** (nothing to deploy, no message).
2. **Strict duplicate check**: exact copies are already dropped. View `sheets/dupes_*.jpg` (new left, existing right): same scene/moment, burst frames, crops, re-posts = skip. Doubt = skip.
3. **Theme judgement by viewing**: view every `sheets/pending_*.jpg` (open originals for borderline) and judge against `theme` in `config.json` plus what the owner excluded (see your memory of their setup). Write `decisions.json` with every `n` -> `"skip"` or a short category label.
4. **Add**: `python3 gallery.py apply decisions.json`. All photos (including skipped) are recorded so they never reappear. Existing tiles stay exactly in place; new ones replace repeat tiles or grow the shape; count text, tiles.json, atlas and card are regenerated from the real count. If nothing was kept, no rebuild happens -> stop silently. If it says `grid is full`: `python3 gallery.py build --regrid` (reshuffles into a larger grid) and mention it in the report.
5. **Verify + deploy**: `python3 gallery.py verify` (must say OK) then `python3 gallery.py deploy` (deploys, then live-checks: 200s, correct count on `/`, `/play`, `tiles.json`, card.png identical, og tags).
6. **Failure / rollback**: if apply, verify, deploy or live-check fails: `python3 gallery.py rollback` (restores previous state and rebuilds), `python3 gallery.py deploy` to put the known-good site back, `live-check` again; append what happened to `~/gallery/update.log`. Only if the live site is still wrong, tell the owner in plain words. Login expired (`vercel whoami` fails) -> tell the owner you need them to sign in again (do the login handoff from `build-mosaic-gallery` section 6).
7. **Report** (only when photos were added), one short message to the owner: how many were added and the new total, 1-2 of the new photos or a sentence on what they were, the live link, and anything unusual (regrid, skipped near-duplicates worth knowing). Example: "Added 3 new photos to your gallery tonight (now 142): two sunset shots and one beach walk. https://your-gallery.vercel.app".
8. Clean up: `rm -f ~/gallery/pending_raw.json`; keep `photos/`, `manifest.json`, `backup/`.

## Creating the routine
After the first deploy, create a scheduled routine/automation with your scheduler tool (daily, at the owner's chosen time in their time zone, default 8:00 PM; state the time zone explicitly), using this prompt as its instruction. Save the routine id and time in memory; to change time or stop, edit/delete the routine. Run it once manually to confirm it works silently with no new photos.

**Routine prompt:**
```text
Every evening, check whether my owner has posted or sent new photos that belong in their photo-mosaic gallery, and if so add them to the live gallery.
Follow the `daily-gallery-update` skill in ~/gallery: fetch only what is new since the last run, run the strict duplicate check, look at the photos yourself and keep only those that fit the theme I saved for this gallery (respecting what they asked to exclude), add them without moving existing tiles, rebuild with the real photo count, deploy, and confirm the live site is correct (pages load, count and share card match). If anything fails, roll back to the last good version and redeploy it.
Stay silent when there is nothing new or nothing fits. Never ask questions; when unsure about a photo, leave it out.
When photos were added, send a short report with how many were added, the new total, and the live link. Send the report to the owner in this chat.
```

skills.name: build-mosaic-gallery
skills.description: Use when you need to create, rebuild, preview or deploy a photo-mosaic gallery website (photos arranged as a shape such as a heart, circle, star, state outline or initials) from an owner's photos - X/Twitter posts, a folder, chat uploads or a Drive/Photos export. Contains the complete tested code (gallery.py + template.html), the exact commands, and the checks. Used by gallery-getting-started (first build) and daily-gallery-update (incremental).
